clinician.trajectory_summary: A 45-year-old male presented with chronic neurological symptoms including imbalance, diplopia, and slurred speech, alongside a chronic skin lesion on his right scapular region. Histopathology of the skin lesion revealed proliferation of histiocytic cells (E002). Immunohistochemistry confirmed Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis (LCH) with positive CD1A, S100, and langerin markers (E003). Brain MRI showed diffuse encephalic volumetric reduction and multiple hyperintense lesions in T2 and Flair, primarily in the cerebellar bridge and peduncles, initially considered unspecific (E001). The confirmed LCH diagnosis was ultimately determined to explain the patient's neurological condition.
